text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency SLO burn detected on /v1/generate for customer-facing route. p99=4.3s (SLO=3.0s). Error budget dropping fast. Triggered auto-page (PD-6329) to eng-oncall-primary.

PagerDuty: Page fired -> eng-oncall-primary. Escalation level: 1. Service: inference-runtime. Pager link: https://pd.example/PD-6329

Jordan: acked. I9m looking into hotpath metrics and recent deploys. Anyone see deploys in last 15m?

Priya: no deploys on runtime in last 30m. I9m seeing a spike in KV cache miss ratio for model-variant a12-quant on eu-west-1. Miss ratio jumped to 78%.

Sam: confirming, autoscaler logs show recent CPU vs queued-requests mismatch. Looks like continuous-batching queue spiked and batchers stalled.

Jordan: ok priority: 1) reduce tail latency for live traffic 2) prevent further paging 3) communicate customer impact. Quick mitigation: shift traffic to compatible variant with lower tail p99.

Priya: I9m going to route 30% of traffic to fallback variant `a12-quant-lite` which has lower memory but faster KV warm path. Patching router now.

Jordan: running command to update routing weight:
```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/routing/update -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","variant_weights":{"a12-quant":0.7,"a12-quant-lite":0.3}}'
```

PagerDuty: Notification: Jordan acknowledged PD-6329.

Sam: while routing change applies, I'm increasing min_replicas for pool `eu-west-a12` to 2 to avoid scale-to-zero coldstarts.

Priya: patching HPA: 
```
kubectl patch hpa eu-west-a12 -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2}}' -n inference
```

Priya: also reducing max_batch_size on that pool from 8 -> 4 to favor lower latency bursts.

Jordan: initial metrics after routing change: p99 for /v1/generate dropped from 4.3s -> 2.9s in 90s. Good. CPU up but within headroom.

Tina: Customer-facing impact: internal tracking shows ~18% of production requests experienced >3s latency during the spike window. No 5xx increase. Keeping product and CS notified with brief.

Jordan: creating short blurb for #product-notify: "We saw a latency spike affecting ~18% of requests for a short window, mitigated by traffic reroute and adjuster. No errors observed; follow-up investigation underway."

Sam: found related log pattern in batcher: 
```
[2026-03-14T11:10:02Z] batcher: stalled on batch_id=0x7f3, waiting for kv-warm: timeout 2000ms
[2026-03-14T11:10:03Z] kv-cache: miss for key=model:a12:prefix_hash
```

Priya: hypothesis: autoscaler allowed too aggressive scale-down and batching semantics caused warm paths to stall (deadzone). Also recent config change to `kv_warm_timeout_ms` made it brittle.

Jordan: action list before handoff:
- keep routing fallback in place for 1 hour
- set min_replicas=2 for eu-west-a12 (done)
- open ticket INF-2897 for config rollback and warmers
- add temporary circuit-breaker to drop queued batches beyond 200ms

Tina: Handoff: I9ll take this for the next shift at 11:30 UTC. Jordan, please add logs and trace ids to INF-2897 and assign to infra-team + runtime.

Jordan: added traces and logs to INF-2897, assigned to Sam and Priya. Also attached small perf dump and the routing patch diff.

PagerDuty: PD-6329 acknowledged and resolved (manual). No further pages to escalation level 2.

incident-bot: NOTE: create post-incident doc in /incidents/INF-2897 within 24h. Set severity to SEV-2.

Tina: final check: p99 stable ~2.8s, p95 ~600ms. I9m closing the page for now, mark follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

Jordan: thanks team. Follow-ups: add warm-up probe to autoscaler, tighten HPA deadzone, and add an eval that simulates KV coldstart.

Sam: will start a PR for the warmers and a small loadtest.

Priya: will draft postmortem and configuration revert plan.

Tina: handing off formally -> next oncall @ 11:30 UTC. Everyone reaction/ack here to confirm handoff.

Jordan: ack
Priya: ack
Sam: ack
Tina: ack
